analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation line added to the environment-variable table of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751). It lists DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES with source AdmissionRateEstimators.swift (DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey). The supplied base units cover earlier parts of the file (lines 1-830), so the changed line itself is not visible as base text; I assessed it from the patch excerpt. The doc-only change adds no code, trust boundary, key handling, attestation path or authorization logic.

The variable name suggests a TTFT admission/deadline scheduling knob. That could in principle touch the TTFT timing oracle (T-041, SEC-035), or availability (T-010, T-029) if the code behind it changes admission behavior. The supplied evidence is only a table row, so that code is not reviewed and no regression can be claimed. It does not appear to alter prefix-cache scoping, the HMAC lookup tags, the TTL, the encryption or the kill switch, but the next pass should confirm this if the corresponding Swift change (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift) is in the PR. The table row also appears not to add launchd forwarding: the context says the table lists variables forwarded to the daemon, so whether this variable is forwarded into launchd is unverified, and any forwarding would be an operator-controlled local setting, not a remote surface.

The base text of the CLI reference is unchanged. It documents logout revocation, the cache settings and the App Attest worker opt-in consistently with the threat model (T-053, T-041). No documentation drift against the canonical model that undermines a stated security control was identified. No findings.
